title: Lesson 35 - License-Driven Design Scenarios: Which Sharing Features Require Which Licenses
description: Given a set of conditions, determine which sharing features are license-required and design the solution within license constraints.

questions.question: An org with only internal Salesforce CRM licenses must give partners portal access to their accounts. What is the key licensing implication?
options: Experience/community licenses (e.g. Partner Community) are required for external users and sharing sets; without them portal access is not possible
questions.explanation: External-user portal access is an Experience Cloud (community) feature requiring the corresponding licenses. Without them, sharing sets/portal access cannot be configured; Shield/Platform licenses do not provide it.

questions.question: An architect proposes Field Audit Trail for 5-year retention. Which license is required?
questions.explanation: Field Audit Trail is a Shield (compliance) feature; it requires the Shield license, independent of the sharing configuration. A permission set cannot grant it without the license.

questions.question: Why must sharing-set-based access be flagged as a licensing concern before design?
options: Sharing sets are an Experience Cloud feature requiring external-user licenses, so internal-only orgs must buy those licenses to use them
questions.explanation: Sharing sets are an Experience Cloud capability for external users; an internal-only license inventory cannot deliver partner access through them without purchasing Experience licenses - a licensing constraint on the design.
